verses.1:1: Proverbs of Solomon, son of David, who reigned in Israel,
verses.1:2: to know wisdom and discipline, and to comprehend words of prudence,
verses.1:3: and to receive turns of words, and to comprehend true righteousness and to make judgment straight,
verses.1:4: so that he may give shrewdness to the innocent, and both discernment and thoughtfulness to a young child.
verses.1:5: For having heard these things, a wise person will be wiser, and the intelligent one will acquire guidance,
verses.1:6: and will comprehend a parable and an obscure word, and sayings of the wise and riddles.
verses.1:7: The beginning of wisdom is the fear of God, and good understanding belongs to all who practice it; and piety toward God is the beginning of discernment, but the ungodly will despise wisdom and discipline.
verses.1:8: Hear, son, the discipline of your father, and do not reject the ordinances of your mother;
verses.1:9: for you will receive a crown of graces on your head, and a golden collar around your neck.
verses.1:10: Son, do not let ungodly men lead you astray, nor consent
verses.1:11: if they urge you, saying, "Come with us, share in blood, and let us hide a righteous man in the earth unjustly,
verses.1:12: and let us swallow him alive like Hades, and let us remove his memory from the earth;
verses.1:13: let us seize his costly property, and let us fill our houses with spoils;
verses.1:14: and cast your lot among us, and let us all acquire a common purse, and let there be one pouch for us."
verses.1:15: Do not walk in a way with them, but turn your foot away from their paths;
verses.1:17: for nets are not spread out unjustly for winged creatures.
verses.1:18: For those themselves who share in murder store up evils for themselves, and the overthrow of lawless men is evil.
verses.1:19: These are the ways of all who carry out lawless deeds; for by ungodliness they are deprived of their own life.
verses.1:20: Wisdom is praised in song in the thoroughfares, and in the squares she speaks with boldness;
verses.1:21: and on the tops of walls she is proclaimed, and at the gates of rulers she sits in attendance, and at the gates of the city she says with confidence,
verses.1:22: "As long as the innocent hold fast to righteousness, they will not be ashamed; but the foolish, being desirers of insolence, having become ungodly, hated discernment,
verses.1:23: and became liable to reproofs. Look, I will put forth to you an utterance of my breath, and I will teach you my word.
verses.1:24: Since I was calling and you did not listen, and I was stretching out words and you were not paying attention,
verses.1:25: but you were making my counsels invalid, and you disobeyed my reproofs;
verses.1:26: therefore I also will laugh at your ruin, and I will exult whenever destruction comes upon you,
verses.1:27: and when turmoil suddenly arrives upon you, and overthrow is present like a storm, and when affliction and siege come upon you, or when destruction comes upon you.
verses.1:28: For it will be that when you call upon me, I will not hear you; evil people will seek me, and will not find me.
verses.1:29: For they hated wisdom, and they did not choose the word of the Lord,
verses.1:30: nor were they willing to pay attention to my counsels, and they sneered at my reproofs.
verses.1:31: Therefore they will eat the fruits of their own way, and they will be filled with their own ungodliness;
verses.1:32: for because they wronged infants, they will be murdered, and scrutiny will destroy the ungodly.
verses.1:33: But the one who listens to me will dwell in hope, and will rest without fear from every evil."
verses.2:1: Son, if you receive the utterance of my commandment and hide it with yourself,
verses.2:2: your ear will listen to wisdom, and you will apply your heart to understanding, and you will apply it for the admonition of your son.
verses.2:3: For if you call upon wisdom and give your voice to understanding,
verses.2:4: and if you seek it like silver and search it out like treasures,
verses.2:5: then you will understand the fear of the Lord, and you will find the knowledge of God.
verses.2:6: For the Lord gives wisdom, and from His presence come knowledge and understanding;
verses.2:7: and He stores up salvation for those who act uprightly; He will shield their journey
verses.2:8: to guard the ways of righteous ordinances, and He will closely guard the way of those who revere Him.
verses.2:9: Then you will understand righteousness and judgment, and you will direct rightly all good courses.
verses.2:10: For if wisdom comes into your mind, and discernment seems good to your soul,
verses.2:11: good counsel will guard you, and holy thoughtfulness will keep you,
verses.2:12: so that it may rescue you from an evil way and from a man who speaks nothing trustworthy.
verses.2:13: Oh, those who forsake straight ways to walk in ways of darkness,
verses.2:14: who delight in evil things and rejoice in evil perversity,
verses.2:15: whose paths are crooked and their tracks are winding,
verses.2:16: so as to make you far from a straight way and a stranger to righteous judgment. Son, do not let evil counsel overtake you,
verses.2:17: which abandons the teaching of youth and has forgotten a divine covenant.
verses.2:18: For it has set its house beside death, and its courses beside Hades with the earthborn;
verses.2:19: all who walk in it will not return, nor will they by any means attain straight paths; for they are not overtaken by years of life.
verses.2:20: For if they had walked good paths, they would have found smooth paths of righteousness.
verses.2:21: For the upright will dwell in the land, and the holy will remain in it;
verses.2:22: the ways of the ungodly will perish from the land, and the lawless will be driven out from it.
verses.3:1: Son, do not forget my statutes, and let your heart keep my sayings.
verses.3:2: For they will add to you length of life and years of life and peace.
verses.3:3: Let acts of mercy and faithfulness not fail you; fasten them upon your neck, and you will find favor.
verses.3:4: And take thought for good things before the Lord and people.
verses.3:5: Be trusting in God with your whole heart, and do not exalt yourself upon your wisdom.
verses.3:6: In all your ways acknowledge her, so that she may cut your ways straight.
verses.3:7: Do not be wise in your own estimation, but fear God and turn aside from every evil.
verses.3:8: Then there will be healing for your body, and care for your bones.
verses.3:9: Honor the Lord from your righteous labors, and offer firstfruits to Him from your fruits of righteousness,
verses.3:10: so that your storehouses may be filled to fullness with grain, and your vats may gush forth with wine.
verses.3:11: Son, do not make light of the discipline of the Lord, nor lose heart when you are reproved by Him.
verses.3:12: For the one whom the Lord loves He reproves, and He flogs every son whom He accepts.
verses.3:13: Blessed is the person who has found wisdom, and the mortal who has seen understanding.
verses.3:14: For it is better to trade for her than for treasures of gold and silver.
verses.3:15: And she is more precious than costly stones; nothing evil will oppose her. She is well known to all who draw near to her, and no precious thing is worthy of her.
verses.3:16: For length of life and years of life are in her right hand, and in her left hand are wealth and glory; righteousness goes forth from her mouth, and she bears law and mercy upon her tongue.
verses.3:17: Her ways are good ways, and all her paths are in peace.
verses.3:18: She is a tree of life to all who hold fast to her, and to those who lean upon her as upon the Lord.
verses.3:19: God founded the earth by wisdom, and prepared the heavens by understanding.
verses.3:20: By perception the depths were broken open, and the clouds poured forth dew.
verses.3:21: Son, do not drift away, but keep my counsel and discernment,
verses.3:22: so that your soul may live, and grace may be around your neck. And there will be healing for your flesh, and care for your bones,
verses.3:23: so that you may walk confidently in peace along all your ways, and your foot will by no means stumble.
verses.3:24: For if you sit, you will be without fear, and if you sleep, you will slumber sweetly.
verses.3:25: And you will not fear terror that comes on, nor onslaughts of the ungodly coming on.
verses.3:26: For the Lord will be over all your ways, and He will plant your foot firmly so that you may not be shaken.
verses.3:27: Do not hold back from doing good to a needy person, whenever your hand is able to help.
verses.3:28: Do not say, "Go back and return, tomorrow I will give," when you are able to do good; for you do not know what the coming day will bring forth.
verses.3:29: Do not devise evil things against your friend, who lives nearby and trusts in you.
verses.3:30: Do not quarrel with a person without cause, so that he may not do some evil to you.
verses.3:31: Do not acquire the reproaches of evil men, nor envy their ways.
verses.3:32: For every lawless person is unclean before the Lord, and he does not sit in council among the righteous.
verses.3:33: The curse of God is in the houses of the ungodly, but the dwellings of the righteous are blessed.
verses.3:34: The Lord opposes the arrogant, but to the humble He gives grace.
verses.3:35: The wise will inherit glory, but the ungodly have exalted dishonor.
verses.4:1: Listen, children, to a father's discipline, and pay attention to know discernment.
verses.4:2: For I give you a good gift; do not forsake my law.
verses.4:3: For I too became a son obedient to a father, and loved in the presence of a mother,
verses.4:4: who spoke and taught me, "Let our word be planted firmly in your heart; guard commandments,
verses.4:5: do not forget, nor overlook the utterance of my mouth,
verses.4:6: nor forsake her, and she will hold fast to you; fall in love with her, and she will keep you.
verses.4:8: Build a rampart around her, and she will exalt you; honor her, so that she may embrace you,
verses.4:9: so that she may give to your head a crown of graces, and shield you with a crown of delight."
verses.4:10: Listen, son, and receive my words, and the years of your life will be multiplied, so that many ways of life may be yours.
verses.4:11: For I teach you ways of wisdom, and I lead you onto straight paths.
verses.4:12: For if you walk, your steps will not be hemmed in; and if you run, you will not grow weary.
verses.4:13: Take hold of my discipline, do not let go, but guard it for yourself for your life.
verses.4:14: Do not enter the ways of the ungodly, nor envy the ways of the lawless.
verses.4:15: In whatever place they make camp, do not go there, but turn aside from them and pass by.
verses.4:16: For they will by no means fall asleep unless they do evil; their sleep has been taken away, and they do not sleep.
verses.4:17: For these feed on food of ungodliness, and they get drunk on lawless wine.
verses.4:18: But the ways of the righteous shine like light; they go forward and give light until the day is established.
verses.4:19: But the ways of the ungodly are dark; they do not know how they stumble.
verses.4:20: Son, pay attention to my utterance, and incline your ear to my words,
verses.4:21: so that your springs may not fail you; guard them in your heart.
verses.4:22: For it is life to those who find it, and healing to all flesh.
verses.4:23: With all watchfulness keep your heart, for from these are the outlets of life.
verses.4:24: Remove from yourself a crooked mouth, and push unjust lips far away from you.
verses.4:25: Let your eyes look at what is straight, and let your eyelids incline to what is just.
verses.4:26: Make straight paths for your feet, and direct your ways straight.
verses.4:27: Do not turn aside to the right nor to the left, but turn your foot away from an evil way. For God knows the ways on the right, but those on the left are twisted; and He Himself will make your paths straight, and He will lead your journeys forward in peace.
verses.5:1: Son, pay attention to my wisdom, and incline your ear to my words,
verses.5:2: so that you may guard good understanding; and the perception of my lips commands you.
verses.5:3: Do not pay attention to a worthless woman; for honey drips from the lips of a woman who is a prostitute, who for a time makes your throat smooth.
verses.5:4: Afterward, however, you will find it more bitter than gall and sharper than a two-edged sword.
verses.5:5: For the feet of folly lead down with death into Hades those who associate with her, and her footsteps are not firmly planted;
verses.5:6: for she does not travel the ways of life, and her paths are slippery and not easily known.
verses.5:7: Now therefore, son, listen to me, and do not make my words void.
verses.5:8: Make your way far from her; do not come near the doors of her houses,
verses.5:9: so that you may not surrender your life to others, and your livelihood to the merciless,
verses.5:10: so that strangers may not be filled with your strength, and your labors may not go into the houses of strangers;
verses.5:11: and you will feel remorse at the end, when the flesh of your body is worn away,
verses.5:12: and you will say, "How I hated discipline, and my heart turned away from reproofs;
verses.5:13: I did not listen to the voice of the one disciplining me and teaching me, nor did I incline my ear;
verses.5:14: I was nearly in every evil in the midst of the assembly and congregation."
verses.5:15: Drink waters from your vessels and from the spring of your wells.
verses.5:16: Do not let waters overflow for you from your spring, but let your waters pass through into your streets.
verses.5:17: Let them belong to you alone, and let no stranger share with you.
verses.5:18: Let your spring of water be your own, and rejoice together with the wife from your youth.
verses.5:19: Let a deer of affection and a foal of your graces keep company with you, and let her who is your own lead you and be with you at all times; for, going about in her affection, you will be very great.
verses.5:20: Do not be much with a strange woman, nor join yourself to the arms of her who is not your own;
verses.5:21: for the ways of a man are before the eyes of God, and He observes all his paths.
verses.5:22: Lawless deeds ensnare a man, and each one is bound fast by the cords of his own sins.
verses.5:23: This one dies with the undisciplined, and from the abundance of his own life he was cast out and perished because of folly.
verses.6:1: Son, if you become guarantor for your friend, you will deliver your hand to an enemy.
verses.6:2: For his own lips are a strong snare to a man, and he is caught by the lips of his own mouth.
verses.6:3: Do, son, what I command you, and save yourself; for you have come into the hands of evil men because of your friend. Do not grow faint, and also spur on your friend for whom you became guarantor.
verses.6:4: Do not give sleep to your eyes, nor slumber with your eyelids,
verses.6:5: so that you may save yourself like a gazelle from nooses and like a bird from a snare.
verses.6:6: Go to the ant, you lazy one, and, seeing its ways, emulate it, and become wiser than it;
verses.6:7: for though it has no farmland, neither having anyone who compels it nor being under a master,
verses.6:8: it prepares its food in summer, and makes its store abundant in the harvest. Or go to the bee and learn what a worker it is, and how noble it makes its work; kings and common people partake of its labors for health, and it is desired by all and renowned. Although it is weak in strength, having honored wisdom, it was advanced.
verses.6:9: How long, lazy one, are you lying down? And when will you rise from sleep?
verses.6:10: A little you sleep, and a little you sit, and a brief while you slumber, and a little you clasp your chest with your hands;
verses.6:11: then poverty comes upon you like an evil traveler, and want like a good runner. But if you are not lazy, your harvest will come like a spring, and want will desert like a bad runner.
verses.6:12: A foolish and lawless man walks ways that are not good;
verses.6:13: and the same man winks with his eye, and signals with his foot, and teaches by gestures of his fingers;
verses.6:14: with a perverted heart he devises evil things at all times; such a one stirs up disturbances for a city.
verses.6:15: For this reason, his destruction comes suddenly, a cutting off and an incurable crushing,
verses.6:16: because he rejoices in all things that God hates, and he is crushed because of impurity of soul:
verses.6:17: the eye of an insolent man, an unjust tongue, hands shedding the blood of a righteous man,
verses.6:18: and a heart devising evil thoughts, and feet hurrying to do evil.
verses.6:19: An unjust witness kindles falsehoods, and sends disputes among brothers.
verses.6:20: Son, keep the laws of your father, and do not reject the ordinances of your mother;
verses.6:21: and bind them upon your soul continually, and fasten them around your neck.
verses.6:22: Whenever you walk, bring it along and let it be with you; and when you sleep, let it guard you, so that when you wake, it may converse with you.
verses.6:23: For a commandment of the law is a lamp and a light; both reproof and discipline are a way of life,
verses.6:24: to guard you from a married woman and from the slander of a strange tongue.
verses.6:25: Do not let desire for beauty conquer you, nor be ensnared by your eyes, nor be carried away by her eyelids.
verses.6:26: For the price of a prostitute is as much as one loaf of bread, but a woman ensnares the precious souls of men.
verses.6:27: Will anyone bind up fire in his lap, and not burn up his garments?
verses.6:28: Or will anyone walk on coals of fire, and not burn up his feet?
verses.6:29: So is the one who goes in to a married woman; he will not go unpunished, nor anyone who touches her.
verses.6:30: It is not surprising if someone is caught stealing, for he steals so that he may fill his soul when he is hungry;
verses.6:31: yet if he is caught, he will repay sevenfold, and by giving all his possessions he will rescue himself.
verses.6:32: But the adulterer, because of a lack of sense, acquires destruction for his soul,
verses.6:33: and endures both pains and disgraces; and his reproach will never be wiped out.
verses.6:34: For the rage of her husband is full of jealousy; he will not spare in the day of judgment;
verses.6:35: he will not exchange the enmity for any ransom, nor will he at all be appeased by many gifts.
verses.7:1: Son, keep my words, and hide my commandments with yourself. Son, honor the Lord and you will be strong, and besides Him do not fear another.
verses.7:2: Keep my commandments and you will live, and my words like the pupils of your eyes.
verses.7:3: Place them around your fingers, and inscribe them on the breadth of your heart.
verses.7:4: Say that wisdom is your sister, and acquire prudence as an acquaintance for yourself,
verses.7:5: so that she may guard you from a strange and wicked woman, if she assails you with words meant to win favor.
verses.7:6: For peering out from a window of her house into the streets,
verses.7:7: whomever she sees among the senseless children, a young man lacking sense,
verses.7:8: passing by near a corner in the passages of her houses and speaking
verses.7:9: in evening darkness, whenever there is nightly and gloomy stillness,
verses.7:10: then the woman meets him, having the appearance of a prostitute, who makes the hearts of young men take flight.
verses.7:11: She is flighty and dissolute, and her feet do not stay still at home.
verses.7:12: For at one time she roams outside, and at another time she lies in ambush in the streets near every corner.
verses.7:13: Then seizing him, she kissed him, and with a shameless face she said to him:
verses.7:14: "I have a peace offering; today I am paying my vows.
verses.7:15: For this reason I came out to meet you; longing for your face, I have found you.
verses.7:16: I have strung my bed with cord, and I have spread it with double-sided coverlets from Egypt.
verses.7:17: I have sprinkled my couch with saffron, and my house with cinnamon.
verses.7:18: Come, and let us enjoy love until dawn; come here, and let us wrap ourselves in passion.
verses.7:19: For my husband is not present at home, but he has gone on a long journey,
verses.7:20: having taken a bundle of silver in his hand; after many days he will return to his house."
verses.7:21: She led him astray with much talk, and with the snares from her lips she drove him off course.
verses.7:22: And he followed after her, lured on, just as an ox is led to slaughter, and just as a dog to bonds,
verses.7:23: or like a stag struck in the liver by an arrow; and he hurries like a bird into a trap, not knowing that he is running for his life.
verses.7:24: Now therefore, son, listen to me, and pay attention to the words of my mouth.
verses.7:25: Do not let your heart turn aside into her ways.
verses.7:26: For having wounded many, she has cast them down, and countless are those whom she has murdered.
verses.7:27: Her house is the ways of Hades, leading down into the chambers of death.
verses.8:1: You will proclaim wisdom, so that prudence may heed you.
verses.8:2: For she is on the high summits, and she stands in the midst of the paths;
verses.8:3: for beside the gates of rulers she sits, and at the entrances she is praised.
verses.8:4: "To you, O men, I call, and I send out my voice to the sons of men.
verses.8:5: Understand shrewdness, you naive ones, and you uninstructed ones, place a heart within yourselves.
verses.8:6: Listen to me, for I will speak noble things, and I will bring out right things from my lips.
verses.8:7: Because my throat will meditate on truth, and lying lips are detested before me.
verses.8:8: All the words of my mouth are with righteousness; there is nothing crooked or twisted in them.
verses.8:9: All are plain to those who understand, and right to those who find knowledge.
verses.8:10: Receive instruction and not silver, and knowledge rather than tested gold.
verses.8:11: For wisdom is better than costly stones, and nothing precious is worthy of her.
verses.8:12: I, wisdom, dwelt in counsel, and I called upon knowledge and thought; for wisdom is better than costly stones.
verses.8:13: The fear of the Lord hates unrighteousness, both insolence and pride, and the ways of wicked people; and I have hated the perverted ways of evil people.
verses.8:14: Mine are counsel and security; mine is prudence, and mine is strength.
verses.8:15: Through me kings reign, and rulers decree righteousness.
verses.8:16: Through me nobles are made great, and sovereigns through me rule the earth.
verses.8:17: I love those who cherish me, and those who seek me will find me.
verses.8:18: Wealth and glory belong to me, and the possession of many things and righteousness.
verses.8:19: It is better to reap fruit from me than gold and precious stone, and my produce is better than choice silver.
verses.8:20: I walk in the ways of righteousness, and in the midst of the paths of justice I go about,
verses.8:21: so that I may apportion property to those who love me, and fill their treasuries with good things. If I declare to you the things that happen day by day, I will remember to recount the things from of old.
verses.8:22: The Lord created me as the beginning of His ways for His works;
verses.8:23: before the age He founded me in the beginning, before He made the earth,
verses.8:24: and before He made the depths, before the springs of the waters emerged,
verses.8:25: before mountains were settled, and before all hills He brings me forth.
verses.8:26: The Lord made lands and uninhabited places, and the inhabited heights of the world under the heavens.
verses.8:27: When He was preparing heaven, I was present with Him, and when He was setting apart His own throne upon the winds.
verses.8:28: And as He was making the clouds above strong, and as He was making the springs of the world under heaven secure,
verses.8:29: and as He was making the foundations of the earth strong,
verses.8:30: I was beside Him, fitting things together; I was the one in whom He delighted, and day by day I rejoiced in His presence at every time,
verses.8:31: when He rejoiced, having completed the inhabited world, and He rejoiced in the sons of men.
verses.8:32: Now therefore, son, listen to me.
verses.8:34: Blessed is the man who will listen to me, and the person who will keep my ways, staying awake at my doors day by day, guarding the posts of my entrances.
verses.8:35: For my exits are exits of life, and goodwill is prepared by the Lord.
verses.8:36: But those who sin against me act impiously against their own souls, and those who hate me love death."
verses.9:1: Wisdom built a house for herself and set seven pillars underneath.
verses.9:2: She slaughtered her sacrifices, mixed her wine into a mixing bowl, and prepared her table.
verses.9:3: She sent out her servants, summoning to the mixing bowl with a lofty proclamation, saying,
verses.9:4: "Whoever is foolish, let him turn aside to me." And to those lacking sense she said,
verses.9:5: "Come, eat of my bread, and drink wine that I have mixed for you;
verses.9:6: abandon foolishness, so that you may reign forever, and seek prudence, and direct understanding in knowledge."
verses.9:7: The one who disciplines evil people will receive dishonor for himself, and one who reproves the ungodly person will reproach himself.
verses.9:8: Do not reprove evil people, so that they will not hate you; reprove a wise person, and he will love you.
verses.9:9: Give a wise person an opportunity, and he will be wiser; inform a righteous person, and he will continue to receive.
verses.9:10: The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and the counsel of holy ones is understanding; for to know the law belongs to a good mind.
verses.9:11: For in this way you will live a long time, and years of your life will be added to you.
verses.9:12: Son, if you become wise for yourself, you will be wise for your neighbors as well; but if you turn out evil, you alone will endure evils. Whoever leans on falsehoods, this one shepherds winds, and the same one will chase flying birds; for he abandoned the ways of his own vineyard, and he has strayed from the tracks of his own farmland; and he passes through a waterless wilderness and a land assigned to parched places, and he gathers barrenness with his hands.
verses.9:13: A foolish and brazen woman comes to lack a morsel, one who does not know shame.
verses.9:14: She sat at the doors of her house on a seat, openly in the streets,
verses.9:15: calling out to those passing by and going straight in their ways:
verses.9:16: "Whoever among you is most foolish, let him turn aside to me; and I urge those lacking prudence, saying,
verses.9:17: 'Partake with pleasure of secret bread, and of sweet stolen water.'"
verses.9:18: But he does not know that the earthborn perish with her, and he comes upon the plank of Hades. Instead, leap away, do not linger in the place, nor fix your eye upon her; for in this way you will cross over foreign water; but abstain from foreign water, and do not drink from a foreign spring, so that you may live a long time, and years of life may be added to you.
verses.10:1: A wise son gladdens a father, but a foolish son is grief to his mother.
verses.10:2: Treasures will not profit the lawless, but righteousness will deliver from death.
verses.10:3: The Lord will not starve a righteous soul, but He will overturn the life of the ungodly.
verses.10:4: Poverty humbles a man, but the hands of courageous men make rich. A disciplined son will be wise, and he will use the foolish one as a servant.
verses.10:5: A sensible son is saved from scorching heat, but a lawless son becomes wind-blighted in the harvest.
verses.10:6: The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of a righteous person, but untimely mourning will cover the mouth of the ungodly.
verses.10:7: The memory of the righteous is with praises, but the name of an ungodly person is extinguished.
verses.10:8: One who is wise in heart will receive commandments, but the one who is unrestrained with his lips, acting crookedly, will be tripped up.
verses.10:9: Whoever walks straightforwardly walks confidently, but the one who perverts his ways will be known.
verses.10:10: The one who winks his eyes with deceit gathers griefs for men, but the one who reproves with openness makes peace.
verses.10:11: A spring of life is in the hand of a righteous person, but destruction will cover the mouth of an ungodly person.
verses.10:12: Hatred stirs up strife, but friendship covers all those who do not love strife;
verses.10:13: with a rod it strikes a senseless man.
verses.10:14: The wise will conceal discernment, but the mouth of a rash person draws near to ruin.
verses.10:15: The property of the rich is a fortified city, but the ruin of the ungodly is poverty.
verses.10:16: The works of the righteous produce life, but the fruits of the ungodly, sins.
verses.10:17: Discipline guards righteous ways of life, but discipline without reproof goes astray.
verses.10:18: Righteous lips cover hostility, but those who utter insults are most foolish.
verses.10:19: From much talking you will not escape sin, but by sparing your lips you will be sensible.
verses.10:20: The tongue of a righteous person is silver refined by fire, but the heart of an ungodly person will fail.
verses.10:21: The lips of the righteous know lofty things, but the foolish die in want.
verses.10:22: The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of a righteous person; it makes rich, and grief in the heart will by no means be added to it.
verses.10:23: In laughter a foolish person practices evil, but wisdom gives birth to prudence for a man.
verses.10:24: In destruction an ungodly person is carried about, but the desire of a righteous person is acceptable.
verses.10:25: When a storm passes by, an ungodly person vanishes, but a righteous person, having turned aside, is saved forever.
verses.10:26: Just as an unripe grape is harmful to teeth and smoke to eyes, so is lawlessness to those who practice it.
verses.10:27: The fear of the Lord adds days, but the years of the ungodly will be diminished.
verses.10:28: Gladness remains long with the righteous, but the hope of the ungodly will perish.
verses.10:29: The fear of the Lord is a stronghold of a devout person, but ruin to those who work evil.
verses.10:30: A righteous person will never give way, but the ungodly will not inhabit the earth.
verses.10:31: The mouth of a righteous person distills wisdom, but the tongue of an unrighteous person will perish completely.
verses.10:32: The lips of righteous men distill graces, but the mouth of the ungodly turns away.
verses.11:1: Deceitful balances are an abomination before the Lord, but a just weight is acceptable to Him.
verses.11:2: Wherever arrogance enters, there also is dishonor; but the mouth of the humble meditates on wisdom.
verses.11:3: When a righteous person dies, he leaves behind regret, but the destruction of the ungodly is swift and rejoiced over.
verses.11:5: Righteousness cuts blameless paths straight, but ungodliness falls into unrighteousness.
verses.11:6: The righteousness of upright men rescues them, but the lawless are caught by their destruction.
verses.11:7: When a righteous man dies, hope does not perish, but the boast of the ungodly perishes.
verses.11:8: A righteous person escapes from a trap, and in his place the ungodly one is handed over.
verses.11:9: In the mouth of the ungodly is a snare for citizens, but the discernment of the righteous is prosperous.
verses.11:10: By the good things of the righteous a city prospers,
verses.11:11: but by the mouths of the ungodly it is overthrown.
verses.11:12: One lacking sense derides citizens, but a prudent man keeps quiet.
verses.11:13: A double-tongued man reveals counsels in an assembly, but one faithful in spirit conceals matters.
verses.11:14: Those who have no guidance fall like leaves, but there is safety in much counsel.
verses.11:15: An evil person does harm whenever he associates with a righteous person, and he hates the sound of security.
verses.11:16: A gracious woman raises up glory for her husband, but a woman who hates what is righteous is a throne of dishonor. The lazy come to lack wealth, but the valiant are supported by wealth.
verses.11:17: A merciful man does good to his soul, but the merciless one destroys his body.
verses.11:18: An ungodly person does unrighteous deeds, but the seed of the righteous is a reward of truth.
verses.11:19: A righteous son is born for life, but the pursuit of an ungodly person leads to death.
verses.11:20: Crooked ways are an abomination to the Lord, but all who are blameless in their ways are acceptable to Him.
verses.11:21: One who places hands in a hand unjustly will not go unpunished, but the one who sows righteousness will receive a trustworthy reward.
verses.11:22: Like an earring in a pig's snout, so is beauty to an evil-minded woman.
verses.11:23: Every desire of the righteous is good, but the hope of the ungodly will perish.
verses.11:24: There are those who, by sowing what is their own, make more; and there are also those who, by gathering, are diminished.
verses.11:25: Every blessed soul is sincere, but a wrathful man is not dignified.
verses.11:26: May the one who withholds grain leave it behind for the nations; but a blessing is on the head of the one who shares.
verses.11:27: One who devises good things seeks good favor, but evil things will overtake the one who seeks them out.
verses.11:28: The one who trusts in wealth, he will fall; but the one who supports the righteous, he will spring up.
verses.11:29: The one who does not get along with his own household will inherit wind, and a fool will serve a prudent person.
verses.11:30: From the fruit of righteousness a tree of life grows, but the souls of the lawless are taken away prematurely.
verses.11:31: If the righteous person is barely saved, where will the ungodly and the sinner appear?
verses.12:1: The one who loves discipline loves discernment, but the one who hates reproofs is a fool.
verses.12:2: Better is the one who has found favor with the Lord, but a lawless man will be passed over in silence.
verses.12:3: A person will not prosper from what is lawless, but the roots of the righteous will not be uprooted.
verses.12:4: A valiant wife is a crown to her husband; but like a worm in wood, so a wife who does evil destroys her husband.
verses.12:5: The thoughts of the righteous are judgments, but the ungodly direct deceits.
verses.12:6: The words of the ungodly are deceitful, but the mouth of the upright will rescue them.
verses.12:7: Wherever an ungodly person turns, he vanishes, but the houses of the righteous remain.
verses.12:8: The mouth of an understanding person is praised by a man, but a sluggish-hearted person is derided.
verses.12:9: Better is a man in dishonor serving himself than one who puts honor on himself and lacks bread.
verses.12:10: A righteous person has compassion on the lives of his livestock, but the affections of the ungodly are merciless.
verses.12:11: The one who works his own land will be filled with bread, but those who pursue vain things are lacking sense. Whoever delights in lingering over wine will leave behind dishonor in his own strongholds.
verses.12:12: The desires of the ungodly are evil, but the roots of the godly are in strongholds.
verses.12:13: Because of the sin of the lips a sinner falls into snares, but a righteous person escapes from them. The one who looks gently will be shown mercy, but the one who confronts others in the gates will crush souls.
verses.12:14: From the fruits of the mouth a man's soul will be filled with good things, and the repayment of his lips will be given to him.
verses.12:15: The ways of fools are right before them, but a wise person listens to counsel.
verses.12:16: A fool declares his anger on the very same day, but a shrewd person conceals his own dishonor.
verses.12:17: A righteous person declares demonstrated faithfulness, but the witness of the unrighteous is deceitful.
verses.12:18: There are those who, as they speak, wound like swords, but the tongues of the wise heal.
verses.12:19: Truthful lips establish testimony, but a hasty witness has an unrighteous tongue.
verses.12:20: Deceit is in the heart of one who devises evil things, but those who desire peace will rejoice.
verses.12:21: Nothing unrighteous will please the righteous person, but the ungodly will be filled with evil things.
verses.12:22: Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord, but the one who does faithful deeds is acceptable with Him.
verses.12:23: An understanding man is a throne of discernment, but the heart of fools will meet with curses.
verses.12:24: The hand of the chosen will rule easily, but the deceitful will be subject to plunder.
verses.12:25: A fearful word troubles the heart of a righteous man, but a good message gladdens him.
verses.12:26: A fair-minded righteous person will be a friend to himself, but evil things will pursue those who sin, and the way of the ungodly will lead them astray.
verses.12:27: A deceitful person will not catch game, but a pure man is a precious possession.
verses.12:28: In the ways of righteousness is life, but the ways of the resentful lead to death.
verses.13:1: A shrewd son is obedient to his father, but a disobedient son is in ruin.
verses.13:2: A good person will eat from the fruits of righteousness, but the souls of the lawless will perish prematurely.
verses.13:3: The one who guards his own mouth preserves his own soul, but the one who is rash with his lips will terrify himself.
verses.13:4: Every idle person is in desires, but the hands of the courageous are in diligence.
verses.13:5: A righteous person hates an unjust word, but an ungodly person is ashamed and will not have boldness.
verses.13:7: There are those who make themselves rich while having nothing, and there are those who humble themselves in great wealth.
verses.13:8: A man's own wealth is a ransom for his soul, but a poor person does not endure a threat.
verses.13:9: There is light for the righteous continually, but the light of the ungodly is extinguished. Deceitful souls go astray in sins, but the righteous have compassion and show mercy.
verses.13:10: An evil person does evil with arrogance, but those who are judges of themselves are wise.
verses.13:11: Wealth hastily acquired with lawlessness becomes less, but the one who gathers for himself with godliness will be multiplied; a righteous person has compassion and lends.
verses.13:12: One who heartily helps those who are beginning is better than the one who promises and leads into hope; for a good desire is a tree of life.
verses.13:13: The one who despises a matter will be despised by it, but the one who fears a commandment, he is well. For a deceitful son there will be nothing good, but for a wise household servant deeds will be prosperous, and his way will be directed straight.
verses.13:14: The law of a wise person is a spring of life, but the senseless person will die by a snare.
verses.13:15: Good understanding gives favor, and to know the law belongs to a good mind, but the ways of those who despise are in ruin.
verses.13:16: Every shrewd person acts with knowledge, but the fool spreads out his own wickedness.
verses.13:17: A reckless king will fall into evils, but a wise messenger will rescue him.
verses.13:18: Discipline removes poverty and dishonor, and the one who guards reproofs will be honored.
verses.13:19: The desires of the godly sweeten the soul, but the works of the ungodly are far from knowledge.
verses.13:20: Walking with the wise, you will be wise, but the one who walks with fools will be known.
verses.13:21: Evils will pursue those who sin, but good things will overtake the righteous.
verses.13:22: A good man will leave an inheritance to his sons' sons, and the wealth of the ungodly is stored up for the righteous.
verses.13:23: The righteous will spend many years in wealth, but the unjust will perish swiftly.
verses.13:24: The one who spares the rod hates his son, but the one who loves him diligently disciplines him.
verses.13:25: A righteous person eats and fills his soul, but the souls of the ungodly are in want.
verses.14:1: Wise women build houses, but the foolish woman demolishes them with her hands.
verses.14:2: The one who walks uprightly fears the Lord, but the one who is crooked in his ways will be dishonored.
verses.14:3: Out of the mouth of fools comes a rod of arrogance, but the lips of the wise guard them.
verses.14:4: Where there are no oxen, the mangers are clean, but where there are abundant crops, the strength of an ox is evident.
verses.14:5: A faithful witness does not lie, but an unjust witness kindles lies.
verses.14:6: You will seek wisdom among evil people and will not find it, but perception is easy among the prudent.
verses.14:7: All things are contrary to a foolish man, but wise lips are weapons of perception.
verses.14:8: The wisdom of the shrewd will recognize their ways, but the folly of fools is in error.
verses.14:9: The houses of the lawless will owe purification, but the houses of the righteous are acceptable.
verses.14:10: A man's heart is sensitive; his soul is sorrowful, yet when he rejoices, he does not mingle with arrogance.
verses.14:11: The houses of the ungodly will be destroyed, but the tents of those who act uprightly will stand.
verses.14:12: There is a way that seems to be right among people, but its end comes to the bottom of Hades.
verses.14:13: In times of gladness sorrow does not mingle, yet joy in the end comes to mourning.
verses.14:14: A reckless-hearted person will be filled with his own ways, and a good man from his thoughts.
verses.14:15: An innocent person believes every word, but a shrewd person comes to repentance.
verses.14:16: A wise person fears and turns away from evil, but the fool, trusting in himself, mingles with a lawless person.
verses.14:17: A quick-tempered person acts without counsel, but a prudent man endures many things.
verses.14:18: Fools will receive wickedness as their share, but the shrewd will hold fast to perception.
verses.14:19: Evil people will slip before the good, and the ungodly will attend the doors of the righteous.
verses.14:20: Friends will hate poor friends, but the friends of the rich are many.
verses.14:21: The one who dishonors the needy sins, but one who shows mercy to the poor is blessed.
verses.14:22: Those who go astray craft evil, but good people craft mercy and truth; craftsmen of evil do not know mercy and faithfulness, but acts of mercy and faithfulness are with good craftsmen.
verses.14:23: In everyone who takes thought there is abundance, but the easygoing and unfeeling person will be in want.
verses.14:24: The crown of the wise is a shrewd person, but the pastime of fools is evil.
verses.14:25: A faithful witness will rescue a soul from evils, but a deceitful person kindles lies.
verses.14:26: In the fear of the Lord there is hope of strength, and for his children he leaves behind a support.
verses.14:27: The command of the Lord is a spring of life, and it causes one to turn away from a snare of death.
verses.14:28: In a numerous nation is the glory of a king, but in a lack of people is the shattering of a ruler.
verses.14:29: A patient man is great in prudence, but the impatient person is strongly foolish.
verses.14:30: A gentle-spirited man is a physician of the heart, but a sensitive heart is a moth to the bones.
verses.14:31: The one who oppresses a needy person provokes the One who made him, but the one who honors Him shows mercy to a poor person.
verses.14:32: In his wickedness an ungodly person will be thrust away, but the one who trusts in his own holiness is righteous.
verses.14:33: In the good heart of a man is wisdom, but in the heart of fools it is not discerned.
verses.14:34: Righteousness lifts up a nation, but sins diminish tribes.
verses.14:35: A discerning servant is acceptable to a king, and by his own adroitness he removes dishonor.
verses.15:1: Anger destroys even the prudent, and a submissive answer turns away wrath, but a painful word stirs up anger.
verses.15:2: The tongue of the wise knows good things, but the mouth of fools will declare evil things.
verses.15:3: In every place are the eyes of the Lord; they keep watch over both the evil and the good.
verses.15:4: Healing of the tongue is a tree of life, and the one who guards it will be filled with spirit.
verses.15:5: A fool mocks a father's discipline, but the one who keeps commands is more shrewd. In abounding righteousness there is great strength, but the ungodly will perish root and all from the earth.
verses.15:6: In the houses of the righteous there is great strength, but the fruits of the ungodly will perish.
verses.15:7: The lips of the wise are bound with perception, but the hearts of fools are not secure.
verses.15:8: The sacrifices of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord, but the prayers of those who act uprightly are acceptable to Him.
verses.15:9: The ways of an ungodly person are an abomination to the Lord, but He loves those who pursue righteousness.
verses.15:10: The discipline of an innocent person is recognized by those who pass by, but those who hate reproofs die shamefully.
verses.15:11: Hades and destruction are manifest before the Lord; how could the hearts of people not be as well?
verses.15:12: An undisciplined person will not love those who reprove him, and he will not associate with the wise.
verses.15:13: When a heart is glad, the face blooms, but when it is in sorrows, it looks gloomy.
verses.15:14: An upright heart seeks perception, but the mouth of the undisciplined will know evil things.
verses.15:15: All the time the eyes of the evil expect evil things, but the good will be at rest continually.
verses.15:16: Better is a small portion with the fear of the Lord than great treasures with a lack of fear.
verses.15:17: Better is hospitality with vegetables in friendship and favor than a serving of calves with enmity.
verses.15:18: A hot-tempered man prepares quarrels, but one who is slow to anger calms even an impending one; a man slow to anger will extinguish disputes, but the ungodly person stirs them up all the more.
verses.15:19: The ways of the idle are strewn with thorns, but those of the courageous are worn smooth.
verses.15:20: A wise son gladdens a father, but a foolish son mocks his mother.
verses.15:21: The paths of a senseless person are lacking in understanding, but a prudent man walks straight.
verses.15:22: Those who do not honor councils postpone plans, but in the hearts of those who take counsel, counsel remains.
verses.15:23: The evil person will by no means obey it, nor will he say anything timely and good for the community.
verses.15:24: The thoughts of a discerning person are ways of life, so that, turning aside from Hades, he may be saved.
verses.15:25: The Lord tears down the houses of the arrogant, but He has established the boundary of a widow.
verses.15:26: An unrighteous thought is an abomination to the Lord, but the sayings of the pure are honorable.
verses.15:27: The bribe-taker destroys himself, but the one who hates taking bribes is saved. By acts of mercy and faithfulness sins are cleansed away, and by the fear of the Lord everyone turns aside from evil.
verses.15:28: The hearts of the righteous meditate on faithfulness, but the mouth of the ungodly answers evil things. The ways of righteous people are acceptable to the Lord, and through them even enemies become friends.
verses.15:29: God is far away from the ungodly, but He listens to the prayers of the righteous. Better is a small gain with righteousness than much produce with unrighteousness. And let a man's heart consider righteous things, so that his steps may be set straight by God.
verses.15:30: An eye that sees good things gladdens a heart, and a good report fattens the bones.
verses.15:32: Whoever rejects discipline hates himself, but the one who keeps reproofs loves his soul.
verses.15:33: The fear of God is discipline and wisdom, and the beginning of glory will answer it.
verses.16:2: All the works of the humble are manifest before God, but the ungodly will perish on an evil day.
verses.16:5: Everyone who is proud in heart is unclean before God, and the one who places hands in a hand unjustly will not be acquitted.
verses.16:7: The beginning of a good way is doing righteous things, and they are more acceptable to God than offering sacrifices.
verses.16:8: The one who seeks the Lord will find knowledge with righteousness, and those who seek Him rightly will find peace.
verses.16:9: All the works of the Lord are with righteousness, and the ungodly person is kept for an evil day.
verses.16:10: An oracle is on the lips of a king, and in judgment his mouth will by no means err.
verses.16:11: The tipping of a scale is righteousness before the Lord, and His works are just weights.
verses.16:12: The one who does evil things is an abomination to a king, for with righteousness a throne of rule is prepared.
verses.16:13: Righteous lips are acceptable to a king, and he loves upright words.
verses.16:14: The wrath of a king is a messenger of death, but a wise man will appease it.
verses.16:15: In the light of life is a king's son, and those acceptable to him are like a late cloud.
verses.16:16: Nests of wisdom are more desirable than gold, and nests of prudence are more desirable than silver.
verses.16:17: The paths of life turn aside from evils, and the ways of righteousness are length of life. The one who receives discipline will be among good things, and the one who keeps reproofs will become wise. Whoever keeps his own ways guards his own soul, and one who loves his life will spare his mouth.
verses.16:18: Before ruin arrogance leads the way, and before a fall, evil-mindedness.
verses.16:19: Better is a gentle-spirited person with humility than one who divides spoils with the arrogant.
verses.16:20: One who is discerning in affairs is a finder of good things, and one who trusts in God is blessed.
verses.16:21: They call the wise and discerning worthless, but those who are sweet in speech will hear more.
verses.16:22: Insight is a spring of life to those who possess it, but the discipline of fools is evil.
verses.16:23: The heart of a wise person will understand the things from his own mouth, and on his lips it will bear good judgment.
verses.16:24: Good words are combs of honey, and its sweetness is healing of the soul.
verses.16:25: There are ways that seem to be right to a man, yet their end looks to the bottom of Hades.
verses.16:26: A man in labors toils for himself and forces away his own destruction; yet the crooked man bears destruction on his own mouth.
verses.16:27: A foolish man digs up evil things for himself, and on his own lips he stores up fire.
verses.16:28: A crooked man sends out evil things, and he will kindle a torch of deceit for evil people, and he separates friends.
verses.16:29: A lawless man tests friends, and leads them away along ways that are not good.
verses.16:30: And fixing his eyes, he devises perverse things, and with his lips he determines all evil things; this one is a furnace of wickedness.
verses.16:31: Old age is a crown of boasting, and it is found in the ways of righteousness.
verses.16:32: Better is a man who is slow to anger than a strong man, and the one who masters anger is better than one who captures a city.
verses.16:33: All things come into the laps of the unrighteous, but from the Lord are all righteous things.
verses.17:1: Better is a morsel with pleasure in peace than a house of many good things and unjust sacrifices with strife.
verses.17:2: A discerning household servant will rule over foolish masters, and among brothers he will divide portions.
verses.17:3: Just as silver and gold are tested in a furnace, so hearts are chosen in the sight of the Lord.
verses.17:4: An evil person listens to the tongue of the lawless, but a righteous person does not pay attention to false lips.
verses.17:5: The one who mocks a poor person provokes the One who made him, and the one who rejoices over someone perishing will not go unpunished; but the one who has compassion will be shown mercy.
verses.17:6: Children's children are a crown of old men, and their fathers are the boast of children. To the faithful person belongs the whole world of wealth, but to the faithless not even an obol.
verses.17:7: Faithful lips will not suit a fool, nor false lips a righteous person.
verses.17:8: Discipline is a reward of favors to those who use it, and wherever it turns, it will prosper.
verses.17:9: The one who conceals wrongdoings seeks friendship, but the one who hates concealing separates friends and relatives.
verses.17:10: A threat crushes the heart of a prudent person, but a fool, though flogged, does not feel it.
verses.17:11: Every evil person stirs up disputes, but the Lord will send out a merciless messenger to him.
verses.17:12: Anxiety will fall upon a discerning man, but fools will ponder evil.
verses.17:13: The one who repays evil for good—evil will not be removed from his house.
verses.17:14: The beginning of righteousness gives authority to words, but dissension and strife precede poverty.
verses.17:15: The one who judges the unrighteous to be righteous, and the righteous to be unrighteous, is unclean and detestable in the sight of God.
verses.17:16: Why does wealth belong to a fool? For one without sense will not be able to acquire wisdom. The one who makes his own house high seeks ruin, and the one who turns crookedly from learning will fall into evil.
verses.17:17: Let a friend be yours at all times, and let brothers be useful in hardships, for they are born for this reason.
verses.17:18: A foolish man claps and rejoices over himself, just as the one who pledges a guarantee for his own friends also does.
verses.17:19: A lover of sin rejoices in quarrels,
verses.17:20: and the hard-hearted person does not meet with good things. A man changeable in tongue will fall into evil,
verses.17:21: and the heart of a fool is grief to the one who possesses it. A father does not rejoice over an undisciplined son, but a prudent son gladdens his mother.
verses.17:22: A joyful heart produces good health, but the bones of a sorrowful man dry up.
verses.17:23: The ways of one who unjustly receives gifts in his bosom do not prosper, and an ungodly person turns aside the ways of righteousness.
verses.17:24: The face of a wise man is perceptive, but the eyes of the fool are on the ends of the earth.
verses.17:25: A foolish son is anger to a father, and grief to her who bore him.
verses.17:26: To penalize a righteous man is not good, nor is it godly to plot against righteous rulers.
verses.17:27: The one who refrains from uttering a harsh word is judicious, and a prudent man is patient.
verses.17:28: To one without understanding who asks for wisdom, wisdom will be credited, and someone who makes himself mute will seem to be prudent.
verses.18:1: A man wishing to separate himself from friends seeks pretexts, and at all times he will be open to reproach.
verses.18:2: One lacking sense has no need of wisdom, for he is led rather by folly.
verses.18:3: When an ungodly person comes into a depth of evils, he shows contempt, and dishonor and reproach come upon him.
verses.18:4: A word in a man's heart is deep water, and a river springs up, and a spring of life.
verses.18:5: To show partiality to an ungodly person is not good, nor is it godly to turn aside justice in judgment.
verses.18:6: The lips of a fool lead him into evil, and his rash mouth calls upon death.
verses.18:7: The mouth of a fool is ruin to him, and his lips are a snare to his soul.
verses.18:8: Fear casts down the lazy, and the souls of the effeminate will go hungry.
verses.18:9: The one who does not heal himself in his works is a brother of the one who destroys himself.
verses.18:10: The name of the Lord is from greatness of strength, and the righteous, running to it, are exalted.
verses.18:11: The property of a rich man is a fortified city, and its glory casts a great shadow.
verses.18:12: Before ruin a man's heart is lifted up, and before glory it is humbled.
verses.18:13: The one who answers a matter before hearing—it is folly and reproach to him.
verses.18:14: A prudent servant calms a man's anger, but who will endure a fainthearted man?
verses.18:15: The heart of a prudent person acquires discernment, and the ears of the wise seek understanding.
verses.18:16: A person's gift makes room for him, and seats him beside rulers.
verses.18:17: A righteous person is his own accuser in the opening speech; and when the adversary attacks, he is refuted.
verses.18:18: A silent person puts an end to disputes, and among powers he sets boundaries.
verses.18:19: A brother helped by a brother is like a fortified and high city, and is strong just like a firmly founded palace.
verses.18:20: From the fruits of the mouth a man fills his stomach, and from the fruits of his lips he will be filled.
verses.18:21: Death and life are in the hand of the tongue, and those who master it will eat its fruits.
verses.18:22: The one who has found a good wife has found favors, and has received cheerfulness from God; the one who casts out a good wife casts out good things, and the one who keeps an adulteress is foolish and ungodly.
verses.19:3: The foolishness of a man destroys his ways, yet he blames God in his heart.
verses.19:4: Wealth adds many friends, but the poor man is abandoned even by the friend he has.
verses.19:5: A false witness will not remain unpunished, and the one who accuses unjustly will not escape.
verses.19:6: Many court the faces of kings, but every evil person becomes a reproach to a man.
verses.19:7: Everyone who hates a poor brother will also be far from friendship. Good insight will draw near to those who know it, and a prudent man will find it. The one who does much evil brings wickedness to completion, and the one who provokes words will not be saved.
verses.19:8: The one who acquires prudence loves himself, and the one who keeps prudence will find good things.
verses.19:9: A false witness will not remain unpunished, and whoever kindles wickedness will perish by it.
verses.19:10: Luxury is not beneficial for a fool, nor if a household servant begins to rule with insolence.
verses.19:11: A merciful man is patient, and his boast comes upon lawbreakers.
verses.19:12: A king's threat is like the roaring of a lion, and just as dew upon grass, so is his cheerfulness.
verses.19:13: A foolish son is a shame to a father; vows from the wages of a prostitute are not pure.
verses.19:14: Fathers apportion house and property to children, but from God a wife is joined to a husband.
verses.19:15: Cowardice grips an effeminate man, and the soul of an idle person will hunger.
verses.19:16: The one who keeps a commandment guards his own soul, but the one who despises his own ways will perish.
verses.19:17: The one who shows mercy to a poor man lends to God, and according to his gift it will be repaid to him.
verses.19:18: Discipline your son, for in this way he will be hopeful, yet do not be carried away in your soul to abuse.
verses.19:19: An evil-minded man will be penalized; and if he acts like a scoundrel, he will also add his own soul.
verses.19:20: Listen, son, to the discipline of your father, so that you may become wise in your latter days.
verses.19:21: Many thoughts are in a man's heart, but the counsel of the Lord remains forever.
verses.19:22: Mercy is fruit for a man, and a righteous poor man is better than a lying rich man.
verses.19:23: The fear of the Lord leads to life for a man, but the one without fear will lodge in places where knowledge is not attended to.
verses.19:24: The one who hides his hands in his bosom unjustly will by no means even bring them to his mouth.
verses.19:25: When a scoundrel is whipped, a fool becomes shrewder; and if you reprove a prudent man, he will understand discernment.
verses.19:26: The one who dishonors his father and drives away his mother will be put to shame and will be an object of reproach.
verses.19:27: A son who ceases to keep a father's discipline will meditate on evil sayings.
verses.19:28: The one who stands guarantor for a foolish child treats a just decree with insolence, and the mouth of the ungodly will swallow down judgments.
verses.19:29: Whips are prepared for the unrestrained, and punishments likewise for fools.
verses.20:1: Wine is unrestrained and drunkenness is insolent, and every fool gets entangled in such things.
verses.20:2: A king's threat does not differ from a lion's wrath, and the one who provokes him sins against his own soul.
verses.20:3: It is glory for a man to turn away from insults, but every fool gets entangled in such things.
verses.20:4: When reproached, a lazy man is not ashamed; likewise also the one who borrows grain at harvest.
verses.20:5: Counsel in a man's heart is deep water, yet a prudent man will draw it out.
verses.20:6: A human being is a great thing, and a merciful man is precious, but a faithful man is a hard task to find.
verses.20:7: The one who conducts himself blamelessly in righteousness will leave his children blessed.
verses.20:8: Whenever a righteous king sits on a throne, nothing evil stands in opposition before his eyes.
verses.20:9: Who will boast of having a pure heart? Or who will boldly claim to be clean from sins? The lamp of the one who speaks evil of father or mother will be extinguished, and the pupils of his eyes will see darkness. A portion hastily pursued at first will not be blessed in the end. Do not say, "I will take vengeance on the enemy," but wait for the Lord, so that He may help you.
verses.20:10: A large weight and a small one, and double measures: both of them are unclean before the Lord.
verses.20:11: And the one who makes them will be tripped up in his practices; a young man is with a devout person, and his way is straight.
verses.20:12: An ear hears and an eye sees; both of them are works of the Lord.
verses.20:13: Do not love to slander, so that you may not be removed; open your eyes wide and be filled with bread.
verses.20:23: A double weight is an abomination to the Lord, and a deceitful scale is not good before Him.
verses.20:24: From the Lord a man's steps are directed, and how could a mortal understand his ways?
verses.20:25: It is a snare for a man to consecrate something of his own hastily, for after making a vow, regret occurs.
verses.20:26: A wise king is a winnower of the ungodly, and he will lay a wheel upon them.
verses.20:27: The breath of human beings is the light of the Lord, who searches the inner chambers of the belly.
verses.20:28: Mercy and truth are a guard for a king, and they will surround his throne in righteousness.
verses.20:29: Wisdom is an ornament for young men, and gray hair is the glory of older men.
verses.20:30: Bruises and fractures meet evil people, and blows reach into the inner chambers of the belly.
verses.21:1: Just as a rush of water, so is the heart of a king in the hand of God; wherever He wishes to turn, there He inclines it.
verses.21:2: Every man appears righteous to himself, but the Lord directs hearts.
verses.21:3: Doing what is righteous and being truthful are more pleasing to God than the blood of sacrifices.
verses.21:4: A bold-hearted person is haughty in insolence, and the lamp of the ungodly is sin.
verses.21:6: He who produces treasures with a lying tongue pursues futile things to the snares of death.
verses.21:7: Destruction will lodge as a guest with the ungodly, for they do not wish to practice what is righteous.
verses.21:8: To the crooked, God sends crooked ways, for His works are pure and upright.
verses.21:9: It is better to dwell on a corner in the open air than in whitewashed rooms with unrighteousness and in a shared house.
verses.21:10: The soul of an ungodly person will not be shown mercy by any human being.
verses.21:11: When an unrestrained person is punished, the evil person becomes more shrewd, and when a wise person understands, he will receive knowledge.
verses.21:12: A righteous person understands the hearts of the ungodly and despises the ungodly in evil things.
verses.21:13: He who stops up his ears so as not to listen to a weak person will himself also call out, and there will be no one who listens.
verses.21:14: A secret gift overturns anger, but he who is sparing with gifts stirs up strong wrath.
verses.21:15: The gladness of the righteous does justice, but a devout person is unclean among evildoers.
verses.21:16: A man wandering from the way of righteousness will rest in the assembly of giants.
verses.21:17: A man in want loves gladness, loving wine and oil for wealth.
verses.21:18: And a lawless person is an expiation for a righteous person.
verses.21:19: It is better to dwell in the wilderness than with a woman who is sharp-tongued and quarrelsome and quick-tempered.
verses.21:20: A desirable treasure will rest upon the mouth of a wise person, but foolish men will swallow it up.
verses.21:21: The way of righteousness and mercy will find life and glory.
verses.21:22: A wise person scaled fortified cities and tore down the stronghold in which the ungodly had trusted.
verses.21:23: He who guards his mouth and tongue preserves his soul from distress.
verses.21:24: One who is brazen and self-willed and boastful is called a pest, and he who holds a grudge is a transgressor.
verses.21:25: Desires kill a sluggard, for his hands do not choose to do anything.
verses.21:26: An ungodly person desires evil desires all day long, but the righteous person shows mercy and has compassion unsparingly.
verses.21:27: Sacrifices of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord, for indeed they offer them unlawfully.
verses.21:28: A false witness will perish, but an obedient man will speak guardedly.
verses.21:29: An ungodly man shamelessly stands firm in countenance, but the upright person himself understands his ways.
verses.21:30: There is no wisdom, there is no courage, there is no counsel for the ungodly.
verses.21:31: A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but help is from the Lord.
verses.22:1: A good name is preferable to great wealth, and good favor is above silver and gold.
verses.22:2: A rich person and a poor person meet one another, and the Lord made them both.
verses.22:3: When a shrewd person sees a wicked person severely punished, he himself is disciplined, but the foolish pass by and are punished.
verses.22:4: The offspring of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and wealth, and glory, and life.
verses.22:5: Thistles and snares are in crooked ways, but he who guards his own soul will keep away from them.
verses.22:7: The rich will rule over the poor, and household servants will lend to their own masters.
verses.22:8: He who sows worthless things will reap evil things, and he will bring to an end the blow of his works. God blesses a cheerful man and a giver, and He will bring to an end the futility of his works.
verses.22:9: He who shows mercy to a poor person will himself be nourished, for he gave of his own loaves to the poor person. He who gives gifts acquires victory and honor, yet he takes away the soul of those who possess them.
verses.22:10: Cast out a pest from a council, and strife will go out with him; for whenever he sits in a council, he dishonors everyone.
verses.22:11: The Lord loves devout hearts, and all blameless people are acceptable to Him; a king shepherds with his lips.
verses.22:12: And the eyes of the Lord preserve perception, but a transgressor despises words.
verses.22:13: A sluggard makes excuses and says, "There is a lion in the roads, and murderers are in the squares."
verses.22:14: The mouth of a transgressor is a deep pit, and he who is hated by the Lord will fall into it. There are evil ways before a man, and he does not love to turn away from them; yet one must turn away from a crooked and evil way.
verses.22:15: Folly is bound to the heart of a youth, but a rod and discipline are far from him.
verses.22:16: He who defrauds a needy person makes his own possessions many, yet he gives to a rich person for less.
verses.22:17: Turn your ear to the words of the wise and hear my word, and apply your heart, so that you may know that they are good.
verses.22:18: And if you place them into your heart, they will gladden you together upon your lips,
verses.22:19: so that your hope may be in the Lord, and He may make your way known to you.
verses.22:20: And you also, write them down for yourself threefold for counsel and knowledge upon the breadth of your soul.
verses.22:21: Therefore I teach you a true word and good knowledge to heed, so as to answer words of truth to those who put questions to you.
verses.22:22: Do not oppress a needy person, for he is poor, and do not dishonor a weak person at the gates.
verses.22:23: For the Lord will judge his case, and you will rescue your inviolable soul.
verses.22:24: Do not be a companion to a wrathful man, and do not lodge with a quick-tempered friend,
verses.22:25: so that you do not learn of his ways and take nooses for your soul.
verses.22:26: Do not give yourself as a pledge, feeling shame before someone's face.
verses.22:27: For if he does not have the means to repay, they will take the bedding that is under your sides.
verses.22:28: Do not remove eternal boundaries that your fathers set.
verses.22:29: A man who is observant and sharp in his works must stand before kings, and not stand before sluggish men.
verses.23:1: If you sit down to dine at the table of rulers, consider intelligently the things set before you,
verses.23:2: and put out your hand, knowing that you must prepare such things. But if you are rather insatiable,
verses.23:3: do not desire his delicacies, for these belong to a false life.
verses.23:4: Do not measure yourself against a rich man when you are poor, but by your own insight hold back.
verses.23:5: If you fix your eye upon him, it will fall nowhere; for wings have been prepared for him like those of an eagle, and he returns to the house of the one set over him.
verses.23:6: Do not dine with a grudging man, nor desire his foods;
verses.23:7: for just as if someone were to swallow a hair, so he eats and drinks. And do not bring him in to yourself and eat your morsel with him;
verses.23:8: for he will vomit it up and ruin your fine words.
verses.23:9: Say nothing into the ears of a fool, so that he may never sneer at your discerning words.
verses.23:10: Do not move eternal boundaries, and do not enter into the property of orphans;
verses.23:11: for the One who redeems them is the Lord; He is mighty, and He will judge their case with you.
verses.23:12: Give your heart to discipline, and prepare your ears for words of perception.
verses.23:13: Do not hold back from disciplining a young child, because if you strike him with a rod, he will by no means die;
verses.23:14: for you will strike him with a rod, yet you will rescue his soul from death.
verses.23:15: Son, if your heart becomes wise, you will gladden my heart also,
verses.23:16: and your lips will dwell in words with my lips, if they are upright.
verses.23:17: Do not let your heart envy sinners, but be in the fear of the Lord all day long.
verses.23:18: For if you keep them, you will have offspring, and your hope will not depart.
verses.23:19: Listen, son, and become wise, and direct the thoughts of your heart.
verses.23:20: Do not be a wine-drinker, nor reach out for shared feasts, purchases of meat;
verses.23:21: for every drunkard and fornicator will become poor, and every drowsy person will clothe himself in torn and ragged clothing.
verses.23:22: Listen, son, to the father who fathered you, and do not show contempt because your mother has grown old.
verses.23:24: A righteous father nurtures well, and over a wise son his soul is glad.
verses.23:25: Let your father and mother be glad over you, and let her who gave birth to you rejoice.
verses.23:26: Give me your heart, son, and let your eyes keep my ways.
verses.23:27: For a foreign house is a perforated jar and a narrow foreign well.
verses.23:28: For this one will swiftly perish, and every lawless person will be consumed.
verses.23:29: Who has woe? Who has uproar? Who has judgment? And who has unpleasantness and chatter? Who has bruises for nothing? Whose eyes are black-and-blue?
verses.23:30: Is it not those who linger over wines? Is it not those who track down where drinking-parties take place? Do not get drunk on wines, but converse with righteous people, and converse on walks;
verses.23:31: for if you give your eyes to the bowls and the cups, afterward you will walk around more naked than a pestle;
verses.23:32: but in the end, like one struck by a serpent, he is stretched out, and as by a horned viper, the venom spreads through him.
verses.23:33: When your eyes see a foreign woman, then your mouth will speak crooked things,
verses.23:34: and you will lie down as in the heart of the sea, and like a helmsman in a great surge.
verses.23:35: And you will say, "They are striking me, and I felt no pain, and they mocked me, yet I did not know it; when will it be dawn, so that I may go and seek those with whom I will meet?"
verses.24:1: Son, do not envy evil men, nor desire to be with them;
verses.24:2: for their heart meditates on falsehoods, and their lips speak troubles.
verses.24:3: With wisdom a house is built, and with understanding it is set upright;
verses.24:4: with perception storerooms are filled with all precious and fine wealth.
verses.24:5: A wise man is better than a strong man, and a man who has prudence is better than a large farm.
verses.24:6: With guidance war is waged, and help is with a heart given to counsel.
verses.24:7: Wisdom and good insight are in the gates of the wise; the wise do not turn aside from the mouth of the Lord,
verses.24:8: but they deliberate in councils. Death meets the undisciplined,
verses.24:9: and a fool dies in sins. And impurity will be stained into a pestilent man
verses.24:10: in an evil day and in a day of affliction, until he fails.
verses.24:11: Rescue those being led to death, and ransom those being killed; do not hold back.
verses.24:12: And if you say, "I do not know this man," know that the Lord knows the hearts of all; and the One who formed breath for all Himself knows all things, who repays each one according to his works.
verses.24:13: Eat honey, son, for honeycomb is good, so that your throat may be sweetened.
verses.24:14: In this way you will perceive wisdom in your soul; for if you find it, your end will be good, and hope will not forsake you.
verses.24:15: Do not bring an ungodly man to the pasture of the righteous, nor be deceived by the filling of the belly.
verses.24:16: For seven times a righteous man will fall and rise up, but the ungodly will grow weak in evils.
verses.24:17: If your enemy falls, do not rejoice over him, and at his stumbling do not exalt yourself;
verses.24:18: because the Lord will see and it will not please Him, and He will turn His wrath away from him.
verses.24:19: Do not rejoice over evildoers, nor envy sinners;
verses.24:20: for there will by no means be offspring for a wicked man, and the lamp of the ungodly will be extinguished.
verses.24:21: Fear God, son, and the king, and do not disobey either of them;
verses.24:22: for suddenly they will punish the ungodly, and who will know the punishments of both? A son who guards a word will be free from destruction, and receiving it, he has received it. Let no falsehood be spoken from a tongue to a king, and let no falsehood go forth from his tongue. A king's tongue is a sword, and not of flesh; and whoever is handed over will be crushed. For if his wrath is sharpened, it consumes people along with their sinews, and devours the bones of people, and burns them up like a flame, so that they are inedible for the young of eagles.
verses.24:23: And these things I say to you, the wise, to recognize: to show deference to a person in judgment is not good.
verses.24:24: The one who says of the ungodly man, "He is righteous," will be cursed by peoples and hated among nations;
verses.24:25: but those who rebuke will appear better, and upon them a blessing will come.
verses.24:26: And people will kiss lips that answer good words.
verses.24:27: Prepare your works for going out, and make yourself ready for the field, and walk behind me, and you will rebuild your house.
verses.24:28: Do not be a false witness against your fellow citizen, nor open wide with your lips.
verses.24:29: Do not say, "Just as he treated me, I will treat him, and I will pay him back for how he wronged me."
verses.24:30: Like a farm is a foolish man, and like a vineyard is a person lacking sense;
verses.24:31: if you leave him alone, he will become wasteland and run wholly wild with weeds, and he becomes abandoned, and his walls of stone are torn down.
verses.24:32: Afterward I repented; I looked closely to choose discipline.
verses.24:33: A little I doze, and a little I sleep soundly, and a little I clasp my chest with my hands;
verses.24:34: and if you do this, your poverty will come walking ahead, and your want like a good runner.
verses.25:1: These are the unarranged instructions of Solomon, which the friends of Hezekiah, the king of Judea, copied out.
verses.25:2: The glory of God conceals a word, but the glory of a king honors matters.
verses.25:3: Heaven is high, and the earth is deep, and the heart of a king is beyond scrutiny.
verses.25:4: Strike impure silver, and all of it will be purified clean.
verses.25:5: Kill the ungodly from the presence of a king, and his throne will prosper in righteousness.
verses.25:6: Do not boast before a king, nor take your stand in the places of rulers.
verses.25:7: For it is better for you to be told, "Come up to me," than for you to be humbled in the presence of a ruler. Speak what your eyes have seen.
verses.25:8: Do not rush into a quarrel quickly, so that you do not regret it in the end, whenever your own friend reproaches you.
verses.25:9: Withdraw backward; do not show contempt,
verses.25:10: otherwise your friend may reproach you, and your quarrel and your enmity will not depart, but will be equal to death for you. Grace and friendship set free; keep them for yourself, so that you do not become subject to reproach, but guard your ways amicably.
verses.25:11: A golden apple in a necklace of sardius—so it is to speak a word.
verses.25:12: A wise word is fastened to an attentive ear as a golden earring and a precious sardius.
verses.25:13: Just as a going out in harvest during scorching heat helps, so a faithful messenger helps those who sent him; for he helps the souls of those who employ him.
verses.25:14: Just as winds and clouds and rains are most conspicuous, so is the one who boasts of a false gift.
verses.25:15: In patience there is prosperity for kings, and a soft tongue crushes bones.
verses.25:16: When you find honey, eat what is sufficient, so that you do not become sated and vomit.
verses.25:17: Rarely bring your foot to your own friend, so that he does not become sated with you and hate you.
verses.25:18: A club and a sword and a pointed arrow—so also is a man who gives false testimony against his friend.
verses.25:19: The way of an evil person and the foot of a lawless person will perish on an evil day.
verses.25:20: Just as vinegar is harmful to a wound, so an affliction falling on the body grieves the heart. Just as a moth in a garment and a worm in wood, so the grief of a man harms the heart.
